description:
The Play: At Ferrari the sticker price is only the opening move: bespoke fittings, factory ceremonies, and year-long waitlists reframe cost as honor. Each upgrade is wrapped in heritage, turning routine add-ons into coveted heirlooms. Scarcity is scripted so buyers feel chosen, not charged. Margin swells invisibly, yet enthusiasm rises in equal measure. Drivers leave Maranello lighter in cash but certain they have won.

The Breakdown: Wealth signals warp value more than horsepower; by controlling context—scarcity, story, ceremony—Ferrari converts markup into meaning. When shoppers purchase identity, price becomes narrative rather than number. That is a legal scam disguised as luxury, and consumers applaud it — Market Mojo.

The Credit: FLETCHERWILSON
